key_insight: A multimodal multiomics machine-learning framework can combine clinical, imaging, and biofluid data to identify and rank biomarkers for faster, more objective tracking of rare childhood neurological disease progression.
clinical_relevance: The approach could improve trial readiness by providing quantitative measures of severity and progression that may help standardize patient stratification and outcome assessment in ultra-rare disorders.
method: Built a large international natural history cohort of 310 patients with PLA2G6-associated neurodegeneration (PLAN).
Integrated disease rating scales, longitudinal neuroimaging, and multiomic biomarker data into a machine-learning pipeline.
Created a clinically intuitive Digital Disease Dashboard to visualize disease severity in real time.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong correlations between disease measures and age, including CoPLAN-DRS (rho = 0.69), MRI Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (rho = 0.96), and neurofilament light with progression (rho = -0.74).
watch_item: Findings come from a rare-disease cohort and need further validation before biomarkers or the dashboard can be generalized across sites and used in routine care or trials.
paper_title: A Multimodal Multiomics Machine Learning (MMM) approach for biomarker discovery and acceleration of clinical trial readiness for childhood-onset neurological disorders
